items.label: AES Q3 FY2025 (11-05-2025)
items.signal_prefix: Data center PPAs: of 8.2 GW signed with data centers, 4.2 GW

set.signal: Data center PPAs: of 8.2 GW signed with data centers, 4.2 GW are in operation and 4 GW in backlog, nearly half of which is under construction and will be added in the next 18 months (excludes utility data center business). PPAs signed year-to-date total 2.2 GW, of which 1.6 GW with data centers; CEO confident of signing 4 GW of new PPAs this year, expecting at least an additional 1.8 GW before year-end as AES is in advanced negotiations on several large projects. CFO: data center PPA returns tend to be at the higher end of the 12% to 15% range because time to power is extremely important. AES Ohio has 2.1 GW of signed data center agreements; at AES Indiana, COO: 'we believe these deals will be more in the 1.5, 2.5 gigawatt range', with AES expecting to be in a position to announce deals in the next couple of months.

items.reason: 1.8 GW is expected additional signings (advanced negotiations are on several large projects), and the Indiana 1.5-2.5 GW range is the COO's hedged belief - attribution and hedge restored

items.signal_prefix: Utilities: AES Indiana partial rate settlement (revenue incr

set.signal: Utilities: AES Indiana partial rate settlement (original revenue increase cut by $105 million, final order expected in Q2 of next year) and IRP filed with scenarios of 520 MW to 2.5 GW of new data center load; Pike County 200 MW storage project online (CEO: the largest energy storage facility in MISO) and 295 MW more capacity by year-end. AES Ohio distribution settlement with an annual revenue increase of approximately $168 million; transmission expected to be 40% of AES Ohio rate base by 2027; utility rate base growth guided at roughly 11%.
set.figure: AES Indiana revenue increase cut $105 million; Indiana IRP 520 MW to 2.5 GW; AES Ohio ~$168 million annual revenue increase; ~11% rate base growth

items.reason: 'Q2 2026' was an inferred date (source: 'Q2 of next year'); 'largest in MISO' is a CEO claim; figure carried AES Ohio 2.1 GW, which belongs to the data-center PPA entry, not this signal
